title: Rocket Report: Lightning strikes in China; Starship launch on deck
gist: A roundup week: India's Skyroot Aerospace reached orbit on its first commercial launch, the Space Force tripled one NSSL launch contract's ceiling to $17 billion (pushing the program past $30 billion combined), Russia's Falcon-9 answer Amur slipped five more years to 2031, and SpaceX prepared a delayed 13th Starship test flight after an engine swap.

insights.claim: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 reached a roughly 280-mile-high orbit on its debut flight, becoming India's first fully commercial satellite launcher to reach orbit.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A successful debut orbital flight establishes India's first credible commercial small-launch competitor, opening a new national entrant in the global small-satellite launch market.
insights.locator: 'India's first private rocket reaches orbit' item

insights.claim: Vikram-1 can carry payloads of up to 770 pounds (350 kilograms) to low-Earth orbit, making it somewhat larger than Rocket Lab's Electron, the world's most successful dedicated small satellite launcher.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A direct payload-capacity comparison to Rocket Lab's Electron positions Vikram-1 as a competitive threat in the same small-launch market segment, relevant for assessing Rocket Lab's competitive moat.

themes.theme: US launch infrastructure and Space Force procurement

insights.claim: The US Interior Department's Bureau of Ocean Energy Management is soliciting public comment on converting some of the hundreds of inactive offshore oil platforms into rocket launch pads, an idea a former FAA commercial space official called 'not as crazy... as you might think' given congestion at existing spaceports.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Offshore launch pad conversion, if pursued, would meaningfully expand US launch capacity and reduce a real bottleneck (spaceport congestion) constraining the pace of the launch market's growth.
insights.quote: It's actually not as crazy of an idea as you might think
insights.locator: George Nield quote, 'US seeks ideas on offshore launch' item

insights.claim: The Sea Launch venture successfully used a converted oil-drilling rig for 36 satellite launches between 1999 and 2014, providing a real precedent for offshore rocket launches.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A proven 15-year historical precedent for offshore launch operations de-risks the offshore-launch-pad concept currently being floated by BOEM.
insights.locator: 'Rockets have launched from a converted oil platform before' sentence

insights.claim: The US Space Force tripled the maximum value of the Lane 1 portion of its National Security Space Launch Phase 3 contract from $5.6 billion to $17 billion, pushing the combined maximum value of Lane 1 and Lane 2 launch contracts above $30 billion.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A tripling of contract ceiling to $17 billion signals materially rising military satellite launch demand, a strong positive read for launch providers holding NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 task orders.
insights.locator: 'Space Force to buy more launches' item

insights.claim: Space Systems Command identified 25 additional Lane 2 NSSL missions in April, on top of the 54 already included in the contract just one year earlier, indicating accelerating procurement volume for the Space Force's most expensive strategic satellite launches.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A rapid, sequential expansion of Lane 2 mission counts within a single year is a leading indicator that Space Force satellite-launch procurement is scaling faster than originally budgeted.

insights.claim: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle, developed in a public-private partnership with DARPA, launched to geosynchronous orbit to begin a decade-long satellite-servicing mission using two robotic arms to install propulsion pods that extend the lives of other satellites.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: The MRV represents the most advanced satellite-servicing spacecraft flown to date, an early proof point for the emerging on-orbit servicing and life-extension market Northrop Grumman is pioneering.
insights.locator: 'Robotic servicing mission launches from Cape Canaveral' item

insights.claim: Relativity Space plans to expand its Cape Canaveral operations, including a new Terran R rocket factory, and add thousands of high-paying jobs in Florida by the end of 2034, though the reporter notes Terran R's officially scheduled first flight by year-end 'is not likely to happen.'
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A long-horizon Florida buildout commitment paired with the author's explicit skepticism about Terran R's near-term launch schedule flags execution/timeline risk for Relativity relative to its stated plans.
insights.quote: That is not likely to happen.
insights.locator: 'Always be scaling' item, Terran R schedule note

themes.theme: Great-power launch pace: US vs. Russia vs. China

insights.claim: Russia's planned reusable Amur-LNG rocket, first announced in 2020 with a targeted 2026 debut, has now slipped to a 2031 first flight, meaning its projected launch date has moved five years later over six years of development.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A rocket meant to answer SpaceX's Falcon 9 slipping to a 2031 debut confirms Russia is falling roughly two decades behind SpaceX in reusable launch capability, a durable competitive gap relevant to assessing Russia's commercial/military launch capacity.

insights.claim: A Long March 3B rocket was struck by lightning shortly after liftoff from China's Xichang Satellite Launch Center while carrying a Tianlian data-relay satellite, but continued its climb to orbit without incident.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Successfully surviving a lightning strike mid-launch, on a rocket with nearly 120 flights since 1996, reinforces the Long March 3B's reliability track record within China's launch program.

insights.claim: SpaceX scrubbed its 13th Starship/Super Heavy test flight on July 16 after some of the booster's 33 Raptor engines failed to ignite at zero, rolling the booster back to swap two engines before returning it to the pad for a Friday relaunch attempt.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A scrub-and-engine-swap cycle on Starship's 13th flight is a normal but material schedule risk indicator for SpaceX's push toward an orbital Starship flight later this year.
insights.locator: 'SpaceX scrubs Starship launch attempt' item, and article opening

insights.claim: The upcoming 13th Starship test flight will, for the first time, deploy 20 Starlink V3 satellites on a suborbital trajectory as a new test objective, alongside the standard goal of a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Testing real payload deployment (not just mass simulators) on Starship is a concrete step toward operational Starlink V3 launches, a milestone relevant to SpaceX's Starlink capacity expansion timeline.

insights.claim: NASA has begun stacking the Space Launch System rocket for the Artemis III mission at Kennedy Space Center, with the core stage's four RS-25 engines still to be installed and a target of beginning fueling tests by year-end.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Concrete SLS stacking progress toward Artemis III is a schedule proof-point for NASA's crewed lunar program, relevant to timelines for SLS-dependent contractors and the SpaceX/Blue Origin lander programs it will rendezvous with.
insights.locator: 'Artemis III is getting more real' item
